Why rent rolls lie: walk every unit before closing

Years ago a Dallas apartment buyer was in due diligence on a 120 unit property. The seller lived out of state and self-managed through an on-site manager who had been there for years. The rent roll showed 75% occupancy.

When the buyer's team walked every single unit instead of a sample, they found that only 52% of the units were actually occupied. Several "leased" units were empty, and a few were being used for storage.

The lesson, the buyer said, is simple: always walk every unit before you close, and match each door to a lease file and a bank deposit. A sample of 10% would have missed the problem entirely.

They also recommend pulling three months of bank statements and reconciling deposits against the rent roll, because a rent roll is only the seller's claim. The key is to verify cash, not paperwork.

The buyer renegotiated the price down by $1.4 million after presenting the findings to the seller.
